competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample set fulfills all elements of the MATATAG learning competency, which requires students to read and write money in words and using Philippine currency symbols (₱ and PhP) up to ₱10 000, as well as the centavo sign. Writing money in words from symbol notation is directly evaluated in items such as "How is ₱3425 written in words?" and "How is ₱7432 written in words?". Writing money using the peso symbol from words is tested in items like "How is 'four thousand four hundred ten pesos' written using the peso symbol?" and "How is 'nine thousand seven hundred forty-three pesos' written using the peso symbol?". The PhP currency code representation is directly assessed in "How is ₱1325 written using the currency code PhP?". Centavo sign notation and conversion with decimal peso representations are assessed in items such as "How is ₱0.25 written using the centavo sign?" and "How is 25 centavos written as a decimal of a peso using the ₱ symbol?". All requirements of the competency text are fully met.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The samples comprehensively cover every sub-component of the competency across the full curriculum domain. The set covers reading money in standard peso notation to produce words ("How is ₱4314 written in words?", "How is ₱6809 written in words?"), converting written words to standard peso symbol format ("How is 'four hundred eighty-nine pesos' written using the peso symbol?", "How is 'six thousand sixty-eight pesos' written using the peso symbol?"), translating between peso values and the PhP currency code ("How is ₱1325 written using the currency code PhP?"), and translating between decimal peso representations and the centavo sign ("How is ₱0.50 written using the centavo sign?", "How is 50 centavos written as a decimal of a peso using the ₱ symbol?"). The numerical range comprehensively spans centavos (25¢, 50¢), hundreds ("How is 'four hundred fourteen pesos' written using the peso symbol?"), and thousands up to near the ₱10 000 ceiling ("How is ₱9852 written in words?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demand and reading levels are precisely calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 2 learners. The question prompts use direct, concise phrasing without extraneous linguistic barriers or unnecessary distractors. Items such as "How is ₱7220 written in words?" and "How is 'four hundred fourteen pesos' written using the peso symbol?" focus purely on reading and writing representations of monetary values. The notation shifts between words, ₱, PhP, and ¢ are age-appropriate and match the developmental baseline of Grade 3 students.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The problem set demonstrates balanced bidirectional coverage across all required formats and notation systems. It features bidirectional translations between words and peso symbols (e.g., words-to-symbol in "How is 'four thousand four hundred ten pesos' written using the peso symbol?" and symbol-to-words in "How is ₱6809 written in words?"), translations between centavos and decimal peso representations (e.g., "How is ₱0.25 written using the centavo sign?" and "How is 25 centavos written as a decimal of a peso using the ₱ symbol?"), and currency code formatting ("How is ₱1325 written using the currency code PhP?"). A variety of formatters (mcq, read_mcq, cloze, set_fill_in_blank) are represented across these variants.

competency_alignment.rationale: All sampled items strictly align with the scope of the MATATAG learning competency without introducing premature concepts, multi-step operations, or out-of-scope skills. There are no word problems requiring arithmetic operations (+, -, ×, ÷), and no references to foreign currencies or units beyond standard Philippine peso and centavo notations. Questions such as "How is ₱4314 written in words?" and "How is 'nine thousand seven hundred forty-three pesos' written using the peso symbol?" adhere directly and exclusively to the reading and writing of Philippine currency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical scale across all items strictly respects the ₱10 000 upper limit and centavo conventions outlined in the curriculum standard. The sampled amounts include centavo fractions ("How is ₱0.25 written using the centavo sign?", "How is 50 centavos written as a decimal of a peso using the ₱ symbol?"), hundreds ("How is 'four hundred eighty-nine pesos' written using the peso symbol?", "How is 'four hundred fourteen pesos' written using the peso symbol?"), and larger multi-digit values up to near the boundary ("How is ₱7432 written in words?", "How is ₱9852 written in words?"). All numbers are whole peso amounts or valid 25¢/50¢ centavo values, completely within the specified boundary.
